Extract Initial Offset
If set, the offset of the extracted motion channels from the origin is removed and stored as a queryable value on the animation
Root Bone Name
This is the bone that will used for motion extraction. If the specified bone does not exist or is unspecified, it will fall back to looking at the AnimationList parent for a root bone name. If the AnimationList root motion bone is unspecified or doesn't exist, it will fall back to using the first bone without a parent in the skeleton which is the first bone. <br><b>NOTE</b>: The first bone in the skeleton can be controlled via the BoneFlags singleton node
Motion Type
Specify the motion type.  Choices are as follows: <br><b>Single</b>: Extract motion from the first frame of the animation.<br><b>Uniform</b>: Extract motion from every frame in the animation.<br><b>Specified</b>: Specify the frame ranges with which to extract motion.<br>

blend_anim_events
fixed_blend
row_fixed_blend_val
col_fixed_blend_val
Blend Anim Events
By default, only the animation events on the first child animation are considered, if true all animation events which have a non-zero blend weight are used to detect animation events
Fixed Blend
Legacy Compatibility :: Ignores Pose Parameter and always blends with fixed_blend_val.
Specific to how the class CMDL : public IModelRenderHelper sets up pose parameters.
Instead of 0, CMDL uses 0.5 as the default and also provides to API access to set the blend.
This results in all 2D/2D Blends rendered with CMDL using a fixed blend weight of 0.5.
The particle system uses CMDL to render models.
Row Fixed Blend Val
Legacy Compatibility :: Ignores Pose Parameter and always blends with this value.
Specific to how the class CMDL : public IModelRenderHelper sets up pose parameters.
Instead of 0, CMDL uses 0.5 as the default and also provides to API access to set the blend.
This results in all 1D/2D Blends rendered with CMDL using a fixed blend weight of 0.5.
The particle system uses CMDL to render models.
Col Fixed Blend Val
Legacy Compatibility :: Ignores Pose Parameter and always blends with this value.
Specific to how the class CMDL : public IModelRenderHelper sets up pose parameters.
Instead of 0, CMDL uses 0.5 as the default and also provides to API access to set the blend.
This results in all 2D/2D Blends rendered with CMDL using a fixed blend weight of 0.5.
The particle system uses CMDL to render models.

AclParameters
tools/images/modeldoc_editor/outliner_icon_acl.png
Parameters which control the ACL compression for animation.
compression_level
virtual_vertex_distance
translation_constant_threshold
error_threshold
tracks_precision
tracks_constant_threshold
Compression Level
Applies to skeletal animation only.<br><br>Specify how aggressively to attempt to reduce the memory footprint. Higher levels will try more permutations and bit rates. The higher the level, the slower the compression but the smaller the memory footprint. <br><b>NOTE</b>: Currently lowest, low and medium are all equivalent.
Virtual Vertex Distance
Applies to skeletal animation only.<br><br>https://github.com/nfrechette/acl/blob/develop/docs/creating_a_skeleton.md<br><br>The virtual vertex distance is used by the error metric function. It will measure the error of a vertex at that particular distance from the bone in object space. This distance should be large enough to contain the vast majority of the visible vertices skinned on that particular bone. The algorithm ensures that all vertices contained up to this distance will have an error lower than the supplied error threshold in the CompressionSettings. It is generally sufficient for this value to be approximate and it is often safe to use the same value for every bone in humanoid characters. A value of 3cm (or ~1 inch in game units) is good enough for cinematographic quality for most characters. While visible vertices around the torso will often be further away than this, finger tips and facial bones will be closer than that. Because the compressed track data is stored in relative space of the parent bone, any error will accumulate down the hierarchy. This means that in order to keep the leaf bones within that accuracy threshold, all the parent bones in that chain will require even higher accuracy.
Translation Constant Threshold
Threshold value to use when detecting if translation tracks are constant or default. In game units, i.e. inches
Error Threshold
Applies to skeletal animation only.<br><br>See :: https://github.com/nfrechette/acl/blob/develop/docs/compressing_a_raw_clip.md<br><br>The last important setting to choose is the error_threshold. This is used in conjunction with the error metric and the virtual vertex distance from the skeleton in order to guarantee that a certain quality is maintained. A default value of 0.01cm (or ~0.004 inches in game units) is safe to use and it most likely should never be changed unless the units you are using differ. If you do run into issues where compression artifacts are visible, in all likelihood the virtual vertex distance used on the problematic bones is not conservative enough.
Tracks Precision
Applies to morph animation only.<br><br>This is the per component precision threshold to try and attain when optimizing the bit rate. If the error is below the precision threshold, we will remove bits until we reach it without exceeding it. If the error is above the precision threshold, we will add more bits until we lower it underneath. 
Tracks Constant Threshold

Translation Ignore Threshold
Solver Settings
Depends on scale of translation, increase for stability at the cost of accuracy
Rotation Ignore Threshold
acosf() heavily exaggerates floating point precision errors. Threshold is high (1e-2f) for this reason. This can probably stay fixed. Increase for Stability at the cost of Accuracy.
Inverse Threshold
Trainer Settings
Linear system is solved by compute a Pseudo-Inverse via SVD. Set the threshold to zero small singular values instead of inverting them.  Increase for Stability at the cost of Accuracy. 
L2 Regularization
Apply the l2 Regularization (Ridge Regression). Increase for Stability & Smoothness at the cost of Accuracy.
Input (Driver)

Output (Driven)

CModelDocAnimStartLoop
AnimSmoothLoop
Finds the difference between the last frame and the first frame in the animation and blends that difference across the boundary.The specified range is from some negative value( number of frames back from the last frame ) to 0, and from 0 to some positive number of frames after the first frame.  This is useful when building a looping animation out of a portion of a non - looping animation, or even cleaning up a animation that is supposed to loop but has a slight hitch.

CModelDocLocalHierarchy
LocalHierarchy
tools/images/modeldoc_editor/outliner_icon_localhierarchy.png
Local Hierarchy controls the space in which sub-frame interpolation occurs. Normally each bone will use parent space (local space) for sub-frame interpolation between two keyframes. Local Hierarchy allows the interpolation to occur in the space of a different bone or model space (world space). The space of a different bone is useful for switching the hand which is holding an objects, for example. Specifying no bone as the New Parent Bone will result in the interpolation occuring in model space (world space). This is useful if the bone becomes detached from the model, e.g. dropping a weapon. Local Hierarchy only affects how sub-frame interpolation between two key frames occurs. Local Hierarchy does not encode the bone differently at compile time. 
new_parent_bone_name
Whether the local hierarchy will use ease in/out values or just automatically apply for the entire frame range
WORLD

CModelDocMorphParams
MorphParams
Input morph params
disable_morph
include_speed
include_wrinkle
best_fit_atlas
width_target
height_target
cut_min
cut_max
Disable Morph
If true, morph data from this mesh is ignored by the compiler and won't be part of the resulting compiled model.
Include Speed
If true, and speed vertex map values exists, include them in the resulting morph data.
Include Wrinkle
If true, and wrinkle vertex map values exists, include them in the resulting morph data.
Best Fit Atlas
If true, try to pack the morph data into the smallest texture size during compile.  This is a slow operation.
Width Target
Set the target width for the morph texture.  It will automatically grow if necessary.  This is the starting size for the best fit atlas algorithm, setting it close to the best atlas size will speed up compilation if best fit atlas is true.
Height Target
Set the target height for the morph texture.  It will automatically grow if necessary.  This is the starting size for the best fit atlas algorithm, setting it close to the best atlas size will speed up compilation if best fit atlas is true.
Cut Min
Cut Max
